object_description: fragmented stepped volume with an articulated radiating plan
design_condition: The compact, stepped building follows the inhabited hillside, preserves the beech and existing plant structure, and forms distinct gardens and undergrowth spaces around its entrances.

positive.statement: The project fits simply and naturally into the topographical and landscape context through its relatively small footprint.

position.rationale: The compact fragmented stepped building is visible across plan and elevations.

positive.statement: The articulated and radiating plan avoids long built fronts and contributes to good integration into the site.

position.rationale: Radiating arms and fragmented edges are directly identifiable in the top view.

positive.statement: The fragmented volume is precisely articulated with neighboring buildings while preserving and highlighting the beech.

position.rationale: The fragmented volume is placed near the preserved landscape zone inferred around the footprint.

positive.statement: The entrances are clearly identifiable as extensions of adjoining exterior spaces and support easy separation of access.

position.rationale: Entrances are approximated at distinct lower perimeter breaks of the articulated plan.

positive.statement: The relationship between the two halls offers visual transparency throughout the building.

position.rationale: The two halls are approximated as adjacent central zones within the fragmented mass.

positive.statement: The circulation devices are generous and spatially rich, and the program is laid out efficiently.

position.rationale: Circulation is assigned to the central connectors linking the radiating building arms.

positive.statement: The project is rational and economical while respecting regulatory constraints.

position.rationale: The judgment concerns overall organization and economy without one useful spatial referent.

negative.statement: The skylights narrow and suggest insufficient natural light in the lower-floor halls.

position.rationale: Lower halls are assigned to the broad lower portions of the stepped elevations.

negative.statement: The relatively high height of the building, coupled with the reduced attic skylights, limits daylight penetration into the lower floors.

position.rationale: The daylight concern links upper roof openings with the lower stacked building levels.
